notes:
Context: Driftwood is a mid-enterprise SaaS provider for B2B support teams — heavy ticket volume (historical corpus ~30M tickets, growing). Primary ask: build a RAG pipeline that enables ticket deflection via an assistant and a human-in-the-loop support agent augmentation. Key priorities: 1) strict latency SLOs for query+rerank (p50 target <=120ms, p95 <=350ms) for top-5 results; 2) high top-5 precision — reranker must push relevant answers into top-3 for >85% of sampled queries; 3) cost-per-query sensitivity: target <= $0.025 avg (inclusive of ANN + rerank model); 4) indexing scale: cold index ~20-35M vectors, frequent incremental writes (daily batches + low-latency updates for escalations).
- Current stack: Postgres for metadata, OpenSearch for full-text fallback, Pinecone proof-of-concept for embeddings (found cost and tail latency concerns). They run primarily in AWS (us-east-1) but require EU residency for EMEA customers.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML + SCIM, SOC2 level controls, KMS integration for key management, audit log retention for 7+ years. Prefer VPC peering or private deployment; minimal exposure of PII to hosted multi-tenant systems.
- Technical preferences: HNSW ANN with GPU-accelerated L2 inner product for embeddings, but willing to test Redwood's dynamic routing to cheaper CPU variants for low-priority queries. Planning hybrid pipeline: ANN candidate recall -> light-weight transformer reranker (top-50 -> top-5). They want configurable rerank models (small/medium/large) depending on SLOs/cost. Also asked about Redwood's KV prefix caching and persistent KV for conversational sessions to avoid repeated index lookups.
- POC ask: 2-week pilot on 10M-ticket subset. Evaluate on metrics: top-5 precision@5, avg end-to-end latency (ANN + rerank), token and infra cost per query, deflection rate lift vs baseline, and resource utilization. Data for POC will be housed in their VPC; security team requires architecture diagram + encryption at rest transit proof.
- Quotes/feedback: "We need reranking that actually moves the useful answer into the first page — not just a fuzzy match list" (Head of Support). "Tail latency kills agent trust; if the assistant times out, adoption fails" (CTO).
- Decision factors: demonstrable latency at scale, clear committed pricing for dedicated capacity, security sign-off (KMS + VPC), and a migration plan for incremental rewriting of indexes with minimal downtime.
- Internal notes: procurement will only sign if we can show 3-month cost forecast and fallbacks to hosted API for burst traffic.
